verdict.rationale: Homebrew documents project dependency encoding via a Brewfile and `brew bundle install`, which installs to a declared state from one command and works in CI such as GitHub Actions. Exit-code-driven scripting is implied by `brew bundle check || brew bundle install`, and non-interactive use is shown by `NONINTERACTIVE=1` for the installer and `install --yes` in admin scripts. However, exit-code semantics and error reporting are not explicitly documented. Missing for 10: documented exit codes for install/upgrade failures, clear machine-readable error output, explicit non-interactive guarantees for `brew bundle`/`brew upgrade` dependency updates, and independent hands-on corroboration of agent/CI reliability.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can have an agent install and update project dependencies non-interactively, with clear exit codes and errors when something fails

citations.quote: You can use this behaviour in scripts like so: brew bundle check || brew bundle install
one command can set up project dependencies across these environments and in continuous-integration services such as GitHub Actions.
Rather than specifying the `brew` commands you wish to run, you can specify the state you wish to reach.
Use this from administrative scripts when the desktop user manages Homebrew, for example `brew as-console-user install --yes` formula.
